11:53 - Surgery: [STAFF] (Clinical Practitioner Access Role) 
Problem: Frank haematuria (K1973)
History: Pt brought in for review - 
explained it was a review due to recent symptoms he reported and to follow up, 
during routine med review it was discovered he's had 2 x reports with blood - one frank haematuria, second dipstick microscopic haematuria but both MSU x negative for infection. duty of candor-  lack of follow up after the 2nd dipstick haeamturia. 
pt initially rang on duty oncall 5th April with discomfort, frequency of urination and blood in urine, noticed a clot and blood in toilet pan. 
urine was dipped and sent off for MSU, 
rpt urine dip was requested after abx treatment
explained usual procedure in concerns with blood in the urine , frank and microscopic haematuria. pt aware we need to r/o ca and also treat any infection if present. 
1. when pt reported initial MSU form - for request didnt say frank haematuria, MSU got filed as normal , 
2. when patient then brought in sample as requested, MSU was sent off again as "?uti" , clinician not informed of microscopic haematuria so 2nd sample also got filed as normal.
3, when patient queried about results via accurx  - since both samples were filed as normal, got informed by admin staff nothing further needed as samples were normal. 

Graeme felt he also chose to ignore the haematuria, says first episode settled with antibiotics which was reassuring for him, 
but after 1-2 weeks had second episode and felt this was less than before and decided to ignore it. 
was very open and receptive, says he understands due to pressures of the system, explained that we have since thought about failsafes at each of these points, 
usually frank haematuria needs further investigation ,

says now in the last few days starting to creep up slightly? 
feeling well in self otherwise, 
no FH of ca, no FH of prostate issues.
